record.what_it_does: Code hosting, collaboration and CI platform with repos, issues, PRs, Actions.
record.auth_notes: Options: fine-grained/classic PATs, GitHub App (JWT -> installation tokens, or user access tokens via OAuth), OAuth apps, GITHUB_TOKEN in Actions, basic auth for some app endpoints. Password auth is unsupported. A multi-user toolkit would use a GitHub App user-to-server OAuth flow or an OAuth app. GitHub recommends GitHub Apps.
record.access_notes: From my own knowledge, not a page I fetched: free accounts can register OAuth apps and GitHub Apps with no review, and any user can authorize them. Org owners may restrict third-party apps. Some features need paid org plans.
record.api_breadth_notes: Hundreds of REST endpoints across repos, issues, PRs, actions, orgs, users, checks, packages and more. A GraphQL API also exists, but I did not fetch its docs.
record.mcp_notes: https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ (hosted by GitHub); open source at github.com/github/github-mcp-server.
record.blocker_notes: No blocker. Free self-serve OAuth/GitHub Apps. Orgs may require admin approval of the app. A free test account serves as a sandbox.

evidence.quote: GitHub recommends that you use a fine-grained personal access token instead of a personal access token (classic).
Authentication with username and password is not supported.
The remote GitHub MCP Server is hosted by GitHub
Webhooks provide a way for notifications to be delivered to an external web server whenever certain events occur on GitHub.
Each REST API endpoint is documented individually, and the endpoints are categorized by the resource that they primarily affect.

record.needs_human: The OpenAPI spec (github/rest-api-description repo), the GraphQL API and the free app registration come from my own knowledge. I did not fetch pages for them. The sandbox verdict ("no") is also unchecked.
